title: What If We Built a Nuclear Reactor on the Moon? NASA Wants One by 2030

scenes.text: What if we built a nuclear reactor on the Moon? NASA ordered one. Deadline: 2030.
The problem is the night. The Moon turns so slowly that darkness lasts about two Earth weeks. Solar panels sit useless.
So in 2025, NASA's acting chief ordered a 100 kilowatt reactor, more than double the earlier plan, launched by 2030.
Earlier designs had to weigh under six tonnes. The likely site is the south pole, where shadowed craters hold water ice.
China and Russia plan their own nuclear outpost for the mid-2030s. Whoever lands a reactor first could declare a keep-out zone around it.
The Outer Space Treaty says nobody can own the Moon. But it says you must respect others' operations. A reactor is an operation. The land grab is on.

description:
What if we built a nuclear reactor on the Moon? In August 2025 NASA's acting administrator Sean Duffy directed the agency to solicit a 100-kilowatt fission reactor, up from the 40-kilowatt designs contracted in 2022, ready to launch by 2030.
Lunar nights last about two Earth weeks, which makes solar power impractical for a permanent base; the 2022 designs were limited to under six metric tons. China and Russia plan a nuclear-powered lunar outpost for the mid-2030s, and the directive warns that the first nation with a reactor could declare a keep-out zone, something the Outer Space Treaty's 'due regard' clause might allow even though it bans owning territory.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Each of the three 2022 design contracts was worth just 5 million dollars; the real one will cost far more. Would you live next to a reactor on the Moon? Drop your own what-if below.
